newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican industrial action rose Jan-Sept - report.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican industrial action rose Jan-Sept - report.

text.p: Labour mandays lost to industrial action rose in the third quarter, pushing the total of days lost in the nine months to end-September to 1.35 million from 870,000 in the same 1995 period, a strike report said.

But industrial relations consultants Andrew Levy & Associates said in their report the figure was still well below that for the same period of the three years preceding 1995 and was not expected to exceed two million by the end of the year.
In the same period in 1994, 2.5 million mandays were lost, 2.4 million in 1993 and 3.1 million in 1992.

"A contributing factor to this levelling off is the fact that the major wage agreements negotiated at a centralised level were concluded, after lengthy negotiations, without any large-scale industrial action," the report said.
Two strikes which dominated the quarter, together contributing to a loss of 784,000 mandays, were at Rustenburg Platinum mine and in the clothing industry.
Wage disputes again formed the major strike trigger (59%), followed by grievances (35.4%).

The report said it was significant that grievances had contributed such a lot to strikes this year. These had ranged from the introduction of new work methods to objections over the advertising of new positions and tax on bonuses.
"...it could be a signal that workers are generally dissatisfied and do not feel that the union (or government) is delivering to their expectations," it said.
Industries which saw the most industrial action were textile (48%), mining (31.1%) and automobile (11%).
